# EDA Findings (generated by the pipeline)

## 1. `eda_01_class_balance.png`

Only 20.4% of customers churned, so the classes are imbalanced. A model that always predicts 'stays' would already be 79.6% accurate, which is why accuracy alone is misleading and recall/F1 are used to judge models.

## 2. `eda_02_age_by_churn.png`

Churned customers are older (median age 45 vs 36). Churn peaks at 56.0% for ages 50-59 compared with 7.6% for under-30s, so Age is one of the strongest predictors.

## 3. `eda_03_churn_by_products.png`

The relationship is not linear: customers with 2 products churn least (7.6%), 1 product is 27.7%, while 3 products (82.7%) and 4 products (100.0%, only 60 customers) almost always churn. Tree-based models can capture this non-linear pattern better than logistic regression.

## 4. `eda_04_churn_by_geography_gender.png`

Germany has the highest churn (32.4%) versus France (16.2%) and Spain (16.7%). Female customers churn more (25.1%) than male customers (16.5%) in every country. These are sensitive attributes, so the model's errors are checked per group in the fairness analysis.

## 5. `eda_05_activity_balance.png`

Inactive members churn at 26.9% compared with 14.3% for active members. Customers holding a balance churn at 24.1% vs 13.8% for zero-balance customers, which motivates the engineered HasZeroBalance feature.

## 6. `eda_06_correlation_matrix.png`

Strongest linear links with churn: Age (+0.29), IsActiveMember (-0.16), Balance (+0.12). Weakest: Tenure (-0.01), EstimatedSalary (+0.01), HasCrCard (-0.01). No two input features are strongly correlated (largest |r| = 0.30), so multicollinearity is not a concern. Weak linear correlation does not rule out non-linear effects (e.g. NumOfProducts).

## 7. `eda_07_numeric_boxplots.png`

CreditScore: median 653 (stayed) vs 646 (churned); Balance: median 92,073 (stayed) vs 109,349 (churned); EstimatedSalary: median 99,645 (stayed) vs 102,461 (churned); Tenure: median 5 (stayed) vs 5 (churned). CreditScore, EstimatedSalary and Tenure barely differ between the groups, which supports testing a model without the weakest features in the feature-selection experiment.
